enonce_markdown: A force $\mathbf F=(2\mathbf i-3\mathbf j)\ \mathrm N$ acts at the point with position vector $\mathbf r=(4\mathbf i+5\mathbf j)\ \mathrm m$. The moment of $\mathbf F$ about the origin $O$ is
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The moment about $O$ is $\mathbf r\times\mathbf F$ (position vector first). For vectors in the $\mathbf i,\mathbf j$ plane it is along $\mathbf k$ with magnitude $xF_y-yF_x$.

### Solution

$$\mathbf r\times\mathbf F=\bigl[(4)(-3)-(5)(2)\bigr]\mathbf k=(-12-10)\mathbf k=-22\,\mathbf k\ \mathrm{N\,m}.$$

The option $22\mathbf k$ comes from computing $\mathbf F\times\mathbf r$, $-2\mathbf k$ from adding the products instead of subtracting, and $-7$ is the scalar product $\mathbf r\cdot\mathbf F$, which is not a moment.

**Answer: B.**

enonce_markdown: A force of magnitude $40\ \mathrm N$ acts at a point $A$ which is $0.35\ \mathrm m$ from a point $O$. The line of action of the force makes an angle of $50^\circ$ with $OA$. The magnitude of the moment of the force about $O$ is
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The magnitude of the moment about $O$ is $|\mathbf r\times\mathbf F|=rF\sin\theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between $\mathbf r$ (here $OA$) and the line of the force. Equivalently, force $\times$ perpendicular distance from $O$ to the line of action.

### Solution

$$G=40\times0.35\times\sin50^\circ=14\times0.7660\approx10.7\ \mathrm{N\,m}.$$

Using $\cos50^\circ$ gives $9.00$, omitting the angle gives $14.0$, and a calculator in radian mode gives $3.67$.

**Answer: C.**

enonce_markdown: A force $\mathbf F=(2\mathbf i-\mathbf k)\ \mathrm N$ acts at the point with position vector $\mathbf r=(\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+3\mathbf k)\ \mathrm m$. The moment of $\mathbf F$ about the origin, in $\mathrm{N\,m}$, is
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

$\mathbf r\times\mathbf F=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\ r_1&r_2&r_3\\ F_1&F_2&F_3\end{vmatrix}$. The $\mathbf j$ component is $-(r_1F_3-r_3F_1)=r_3F_1-r_1F_3$.

### Solution

$$\mathbf r\times\mathbf F=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\1&2&3\\2&0&-1\end{vmatrix}=\mathbf i\,(2\cdot(-1)-3\cdot0)-\mathbf j\,(1\cdot(-1)-3\cdot2)+\mathbf k\,(1\cdot0-2\cdot2)$$

$$=-2\mathbf i+7\mathbf j-4\mathbf k.$$

The option $2\mathbf i-7\mathbf j+4\mathbf k$ is $\mathbf F\times\mathbf r$; the others come from forgetting the minus sign in front of the $\mathbf j$ term or slipping a sign in the $\mathbf k$ term.

**Answer: D.**

enonce_markdown: A force $\mathbf F_1=(3\mathbf i+\mathbf j)\ \mathrm N$ acts at the point $(2,-1)$ and a force $\mathbf F_2=(-\mathbf i+4\mathbf j)\ \mathrm N$ acts at the point $(1,3)$, where coordinates are in metres. The (anticlockwise) resultant moment of the two forces about the origin is
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

In two dimensions the anticlockwise moment of a force $(F_x,F_y)$ acting at $(x,y)$ about the origin is $xF_y-yF_x$. The moment of a system is the sum of the individual moments.

### Solution

$$G_1=(2)(1)-(-1)(3)=2+3=5,\qquad G_2=(1)(4)-(3)(-1)=4+3=7.$$

$$G=G_1+G_2=12\ \mathrm{N\,m}\ \text{(anticlockwise)}.$$

The value $-12$ reverses the formula; $2$ subtracts $G_1$ from $G_2$; $9$ forgets the $-yF_x$ term in $G_1$.

**Answer: D.**

enonce_markdown: A force $\mathbf F=(3\mathbf i-4\mathbf j)\ \mathrm N$ acts at the point $A(2,1)$, coordinates in metres. Find the moment of $\mathbf F$ about the point $P(-1,3)$, stating its sense, and hence find the perpendicular distance from $P$ to the line of action of $\mathbf F$.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The moment about a point $P$ uses the position vector of the point of application **relative to $P$**: $\mathbf r_{PA}=\mathbf r_A-\mathbf r_P$. Then $G=xF_y-yF_x$ (anticlockwise positive), and $|G|=|\mathbf F|\,d$ where $d$ is the perpendicular distance from $P$ to the line of action.

### Solution

$\mathbf r_{PA}=(2-(-1))\mathbf i+(1-3)\mathbf j=3\mathbf i-2\mathbf j$.

$$G=(3)(-4)-(-2)(3)=-12+6=-6\ \mathrm{N\,m}.$$

The moment has magnitude $6\ \mathrm{N\,m}$ and is **clockwise**.

$|\mathbf F|=\sqrt{3^2+(-4)^2}=5\ \mathrm N$, so

$$d=\frac{|G|}{|\mathbf F|}=\frac65=1.2\ \mathrm m.$$

enonce_markdown:
Three forces act in the $xy$-plane (coordinates in metres):

* $\mathbf F_1=(4\mathbf i+3\mathbf j)\ \mathrm N$ acting at $(0,2)$,
* $\mathbf F_2=(5\mathbf j-\mathbf i)\ \mathrm N$ acting at $(3,0)$,
* $\mathbf F_3=(2\mathbf i-2\mathbf j)\ \mathrm N$ acting at $(1,4)$.

(a) Find the resultant force $\mathbf R$ and its magnitude.

(b) Find the total moment of the three forces about the origin.

(c) The line of action of $\mathbf R$ crosses the $x$-axis at the point $(p,0)$. Find $p$.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The resultant force is the vector sum. A single force $\mathbf R$ is equivalent to the system when it has the same resultant **and** the same moment about every point; so its moment about $O$ must equal the sum of the individual moments.

### Solution

**(a)** $\mathbf R=(4-1+2)\mathbf i+(3+5-2)\mathbf j=5\mathbf i+6\mathbf j$ N, so $|\mathbf R|=\sqrt{25+36}=\sqrt{61}\approx7.81\ \mathrm N$.

**(b)** Using $xF_y-yF_x$ for each force:

$$G_1=0(3)-2(4)=-8,\quad G_2=3(5)-0(-1)=15,\quad G_3=1(-2)-4(2)=-10.$$

Total moment about $O$: $-8+15-10=-3\ \mathrm{N\,m}$ (that is $3\ \mathrm{N\,m}$ clockwise).

**(c)** $\mathbf R$ acting at $(p,0)$ has moment about $O$: $p\cdot6-0\cdot5=6p$. This must equal the total moment:

$$6p=-3\ \Rightarrow\ p=-\tfrac12.$$

The line of action of $\mathbf R$ crosses the $x$-axis at $\left(-\tfrac12,\,0\right)$.
